newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Two Taiwan agents indicted for spying for China.
newsitem.headline: Two Taiwan agents indicted for spying for China.

text.p: Taiwan prosecutors on Friday indicted two former agents of the ruling Nationalist Party on charges of spying for arch rival China, just three days after a businessman was sentenced on similar charges.

Wu Tao-ming, 57, who worked in Macau for the Nationalist Party's Overseas Affairs Department, was charged with gathering information on Chinese communists in violation of national security and military secret laws.

Chang Lu-chung, 61, a retired employee of the Nationalist Party's Mainland Affairs Department, was charged with helping Wu collect military and other confidential information for China, said a copy of the indictment released to the press.
"Wu was bought by the Chinese communists in 1995...and handed confidential information to the Chinese communists, which would seriously affect our national security," the indictment said.
Wu and Chang were tricked into coming to Taiwan by security authorities in February and were arrested at a local hotel.
Under Taiwan laws, Wu could face a life sentence while Chang faces a jail term of up to 10 years if convicted.
Wu was the first Taiwan national to be indicted for serving as a double agent since the island lifted martial law in 1987.
On Tuesday, a Taiwan court sentenced a local businessman to one year in prison for spying for China, indicating a tightening of security by Taipei.
Taiwan and China have remained rivals since they split at the end of a civil war in 1949.
